back: `break` ends the loop immediately, so `"milk"` is the last item checked. The loop variable keeps its last value.
`continue` skips the rest of the body for that round and jumps to the next one, so 3 is not printed but the loop carries on.
It does nothing: it is a placeholder where Python needs at least one line, for example in an empty `if` or loop body you will fill in later.

front: What is the difference between `break` and `continue`?
back: `break` leaves the whole loop, `continue` only skips to the next round. After `break` the program goes on after the loop.
`pass` does nothing, so the loop body runs without any effect and the loop still visits every number. `n` ends at the last value, 2.
